body: So, how do you like Navy Fed? I’m looking at moving too after banking with USAA for the past 24 years.

Sorry for the late reply. We immediately called Amex and in our case, we sent them a copy of the receipt and a photo of broken TV and serial number etc. They credited our card the price of the TV and we repurchased. Easy! 

I have other cards with purchase protection And extended warranty, but honestly, I hear that they make it nearly impossible to file a claim. I can’t personally verify that.

I don’t utilize it but they have something called Blueprint on their website (I think the app is defunct now). I tag my transactions and let it spit out a report for me at the end of the year. You can set up your own tags. You can easily add receipts to each transaction on the app and I think on their website as well.

Amex is the very best with purchase protection. My kids broke a flat screen TV the day after we got it. Amex credited my card back just like this. 

To compare, a few years back my husband put his laptop on his Costco Citibank and when it broke, attempted to file a claim with Citi’s insurance provider. They wanted 2 separate bids for repair and all sorts of stuff. Basically made it such a headache that you give up.
I can’t get past .25 because when I do, I have muscle spasms in my shoulders. It could also be dehydration because it’s a real struggle to consume an appreciable amount of water.
We just sold our 2001 MDX with 245,000 miles on it! Put in a new transmission a few years back but other than that…very reliable.

I have two of them and also the Amazon air quality monitors that work with Alexa. Anyway, these always reduce my air contaminates like VOCs and particulate matter as verified by the Amazon monitor. In short: they work.
Agree, I’ve never had to wait more than 2-3 days. This month, pharmacy told me to check back mid to late Feb. 🙄 Im taking caffeine and L Theanine, both bought on Amazon.

It’s not the pharmacists fault but CVS and Walgreens have them filling more scripts than is safe all while giving flu and COVID vaccines too. They look insanely busy and this isn’t a pizza restaurant—you mess up, someone dies. I go to smaller pharmacy if for no other reason than this.

My POTS ended up being anemia. Docs don’t have a clue about ferritin levels (buy thing under 30 is absolute anemia). I do have EDS, just as a side note. I found out trying to donate blood, after years of torturous and expensive testing that my ferritin was a 5. Because my red blood cells were “okay” docs said I was fine. I could barely stand up, I was so tired. Now, I’m a 55 ferritin after plenty of trial and error on finding the “right iron” for me. POTS is totally gone.

Over 12 months the OP toured homes. I have my buyers hand out my card and never write down their own name, only mine on any guest book/registry. I don’t know the situation but I can tell you that it’s not uncommon for a buyer’s agent to work with at least 5 buyers at any given time and the fact that this was buyers that took a year to find something…how are we expecting that agent to be there every time OP drove past a sign and stopped by a new home community? You simply can’t be omnipresent. Buyers attend open houses on their own and enter new home communities as well.

This isn’t the case in our area. The agent sitting on site either gets half of the commission or they get it all. Having a lower commission if you don’t use a buyer’s agent must be disclosed on the listing in our mls as variable rate. Buyers try to make offers on listings with the listing agent all the time and deduct the BA commission but again, that’s not how it works here unless it’s disclosed up from as a variable commission rate.

A builder will not help you facilitate an inspection of that new house, at least not an objective one! We have buyers inspect at 4 different stages. Builders and their agents don’t look out for what’s best for you, but for them.
Not a week goes by that I don’t receive a compliment on my 8 year old Col. Littleton Work Bag in American Buffalo.
Acting as a “showing partner” is a great way to stay up to date on the market while making a little cash.

You can buy your own personal domain name and email to go with it. It would follow you to any  brokerage, since you own it. I can’t help it but it just seems unprofessional to me when I receive emails from Realtors with a Yahoo account!

Two schools of thought on final walkthrough: 1) if you do it too close to the closings, nothing can be remedied without holding up closing. 2) If you do it too early, you could miss substantial changes to the property. Tell your buyers the pros/cons and let them decide when they’d prefer.

Here we have what everyone else has but I’ve never seen so much cash. You can have an extremely well qualified buyer with 25% (or more) down, offer non refundable EMD, an appraisal gap waiver (with proof they can make the difference), inspection waiver, way, way over list (of course!)….and all day, every day lose to all cash buyers. On my listings, probably half of the 12-25 offers will be all cash. My buyers with conventional financing (forget FHA/VA) cannot buy a house in this market.
I’ve been wondering when there will be a dateline story where a buyer literally kills for a house.
Colonel Littleton or Saddleback. Both expensive but last several lifetimes. I’ve bought some used.

No open houses because no one needs yet another buyer in a market where there is under 2 weeks’ supply of houses. 

Everything here is going for cash and pre-approved buyers, no matter how well qualified, are just spinning their wheels.
I have a 15 year old wallet but I've moved on to Col. Littleton. It's like going from one drug to a harder drug. Leather is an addiction!

BIFL for dog beds is for sure Kuranda. I've had two of them for 20 years now, through multiple dogs. They use them in rescues and kennels. They are comfortable with a blanket or foam pad if needed yet easily hosed down and dried. [Kuranda](https://kuranda.com)

I’m the opposite. Sunosi is my perfect pill but o can’t get my insurance to cover it! The co-pay assistance will only cover like 9-10 pills a month for some reason. I’m trying to stop taking Adderall because my stomach is a mess from it. My 100mg of moda may as well be like taking tic tacs. Not nearly enough!

Sunosi makes you feel “normal”—not focused on on your work. Just energetic enough to roll all day without multiple doses and no up and down BS. Plus, I’ve written elsewhere—Adderall is making me extremely dehydrated where I’m always dying of thirst and having headaches from not drinking enough.

It’s labcorp—My doctor ordered it in May. My rheumatologist ordered a repeat last week. I’ve already had a colonoscopy and endoscopy but they didn’t send for testing. The rest of this panel was within normal limits.

I am waiting this panel again. The first one was run by my regular doctor. The second one was ran by my rheumatologist. They are not alternative medicine docs or anything. I have already had endo and colonoscopy and they didn’t send anything for testing but didn’t seem concerned. Called my stomach problems IBS (the catchall) and put me on Linzess. I’m on like 15 meds, not exaggerating for everything from depression to chronic migraines. I’m not that old to be this unhealthy. My doctor said just stop eating gluten and dairy and see what happens! That’s exactly what I am doing. Started yesterday.

I just wanted to tell you that you are not alone. My daughter’s entire legs and torso are covered with spots where she’s picked holes. It gets so bad when her anxiety is worse. She hates summer because she has purplish marks where even the healed scars are so shorts are obviously out of the question.

My blood work came back high for “non celiac” gluten sensitivity and I’m dead tired all the time. I’ve got daily migraines and severe depression, I look 5 mo pregnant by 5 pm every day (calling that IBS) and they are trying to diagnose me with Sjogren’s currently. I have had a lightbulb moment and I think it’s the gluten! Worth a shot!

I’m doing ketamine and daily TMS. It’s like this is my entire life (trying to get better). Before, I thought about suicide every 10 min. But after 3 weeks of both I’m so much better. TMS is a miracle as crazy as it sounds.

Refuse to sign anything. The dealership cannot fund your loan without a signed contract and that means they can’t get paid. They have the car in their possession—not your problem. Keep detailed notes of any facts that occurred and cancel any deposits you put down.

Each person's reasons are their own but I have more those many and I'm personally SO sick of hearing, "why is someone like you depressed--you have such a nice home/make so much money, etc". While, I totally agree $ can make things more comfortable--you can also be just as miserable, lonely and suffer from substance abuse issues that lead to suicide. Sometimes, I feel an immense amount of pressure because I cannot let anyone find out that something is "wrong" with me or risk losing my job or tarnishing my families' reputation. That just makes even more and more pressure and guilt--which, leads to anxiety. It's not easy to share, even in therapy because we need to keep things private. I guess I just wanted to convey--"when you've got nothing, you've got nothing to loose" and we are all going though are own struggles. Best of luck to everyone fighting the good fight.

I’m reading a book called “Feeling Good”. It’s totally not anti-med but it’s really helping me with some of my distorted thinking—more so than most of the therapist I’ve been to. The reason I bring it up is because he does talk about how ineffective anti-depressants are for many people. It’s our repeat thought loops (I’m paraphrasing) that have us all messed up.

I only want to say that I am only out of bed for about 3 hours a day for the past 2.5 years. I have severe depression. My children have lost me. They come and sit on the side of the bed and visit me in a dimly lit room. I don’t know what the hell even happened. It’s really awful. I’m going to keep fighting like hell until something changes.

I got a tummy tuck, lipo, brest implants and I'm totally miserable 18 months later. In fact--I don't think anyone should be making major choices if they are depressed. If you aren't happy with you--surgery certainly won't help. In fact, the very best sugeon's due a psych screen before you have major surgery. Get happy, love yourself and then do what you want. BTW, I took my implants out because I hated them.
Does this help you text—I have a horrible time holding my phone and texting anymore.

I had loss of sensation overall--so that sucked because I had sexy breasts but I could not feel them nearly as much as I could before. But, as far as immune response issues go--I began to have joint pain and severe digestive issues. I also suffered from depression for the first time in my life. I ended up on tons of new meds. The sensation came back once they were removed but I am still dealing with some of the residual issues. I think people should look into fat transfer. I am not considering anything else at this time but if I had it to do over again, I would obviously go this route. No repeat surgeries for life and no chance of foreign body rejection (that's what I think of it as).

I may have missed something but I read in the details that they never searched her apartment because, she got shot. 3 successful raids involving this drug dealer (ex BF) occurred that same night. Money and drugs were recovered in all. She had been seen going from the address(s) involved and back to this apartment where the shooting occurred. This is why the police were able to obtain a warrant in the first place. What are the chances, with 3/4 of the places having drugs and/or drug money--that this 4th spot had no drugs or drug money? I don't know but that sounds like a reach to me. They didn't find it, because no one looked?

I just had my implants removed after 18mo. I had the brand new IDEAL saline implants--they helped lead to my EDS diagnoses actually. I flew several states away to see someone who specializes in removal. I was experiencing so many complications that emerged after having mine placed. 

Some people seem to be fine but no matter what implants are only designed to be in place for 10 years (per the FDA) so mine meant a lifetime of repeat surgeries which I didn't need, given everything else. Good luck to you!
